newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO panel finds against EU in banana trade row.
newsitem.headline: WTO panel finds against EU in banana trade row.

text.p: A World Trade Organisation (WTO) panel has issued a preliminary ruling that the European Union's banana import regime violates open trading rules, diplomats said on Tuesday.

They said the panel's initial report, issued after several months of deliberations, recommended that the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) ask Brussels to bring the regime into line with its obligations under global trade accords.

The text of the report was not made public but was delivered to the EU and U.S. trade missions in Geneva and to the offices of four Latin American countries who had joined the United States in challenging Brussels on the issue.
The report will be finalised once comments have come in from all six on its findings. The EU can then appeal, extending the process of reaching a settlement in the dispute for several more months.

According to the diplomats, the three panellists found that the controversial regime -- which favours bananas from former European colonies especially in the Caribbean -- went against WTO agreements on trade in goods and services.
"As I see it, the report goes to the heart of the regime. I cannot see how the EU can avoid doing something about bringing it into conformity," said one envoy familiar with the text.
